kimi-k2.5 on 64x h200: kimi-k2-5-h200-multidoc-pd

A deterministic sweep over multidoc traffic, comparing 3 designs on one GPU budget.

BLIS discrete-event simulationExperiment Spec (RFC #21)deterministic sweep — no LLM in the measurement pathseed 42

What was tested

190 configurations over 3 sweeps (colocated, pd-dp1, pd-always), each at 5 load levels, every run on exactly 64 GPUs.

What was found

8x TP4xDP2 + EP (batch tokens 32,768), from the colocated sweep, reached 56.34 tok/s/accelerator (3605.7 tok/s across the fleet) at concurrency 64 while holding the scenario's SLOs.

What to run

8x TP4xDP2 + EP (batch tokens 32,768) at concurrency 64. 368 of 950 runs held the SLOs.

1The measurements

Every run in this experiment is in the explorer below: filter by outcome to see which settings held the SLOs, or by setting to compare one sweep against another.

Each sweep's hypothesis was written before the runs, and is quoted beside that sweep's measured result below.

2Sweep: colocated

The colocated control should hold ITL only with a chunked-prefill cap, and the wide-dp shapes should give the most tokens per GPU.

Measured: best was 8x TP4xDP2 + EP (batch tokens 32,768) at 56.34 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 64).

3Sweep: pd-dp1

Prefill-heavy ratios should win on 10k prompts, and a threshold near the median prompt should beat splitting every request.

Measured: best was 3P/5D TP8 + EP at 55.81 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 64).

4Sweep: pd-always

Splitting every request should cost ITL headroom against the threshold arms, because each handoff stalls a decode slot.

Measured: best was 4P/4D TP8 + EP at 35.9 tok/s/accelerator (concurrency 32).
